title: Curvature-Aware Edge Dynamic GNNs for Low-$p_T$ Track Reconstruction at HL-LHC
abstract: Particle track reconstruction in high-energy collider experiments is a computationally demanding combinatorial problem, traditionally solved by Kalman filters that scale poorly with increasing detector occupancy. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative. In this work, we introduce the Manifold Helical-IN, a novel Interaction Network architecture that explicitly embeds detector spacepoints onto a helical manifold chart using curvature-aware features. This geometric projection mathematically unrolls the tightly curling trajectories of low-momentum particles. Consequently, the network can distinguish true physical tracks from combinatorial noise with good precision. Evaluated on the TrackML challenge dataset, the proposed Manifold Helical-IN achieves a reconstruction efficiency of 0.9675 in the experimentally critical $p_T > 0.5$ GeV regime, approaching recently reported Transformer-based approaches. Crucially, the manifold embedding yields a fake track rate of 0.0037. This represents a 13-fold improvement over the baseline Helical-IN (0.0508). Furthermore, the model maintains good track coherence, as quantified by our proposed Mean Hit Recovery Fraction (MHRF) of 0.858, and achieves a highly efficient inference latency of approximately 150 ms per event on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. These results represent a critical step toward real-time soft particle tracking for the High-Level Trigger (HLT). By operating within practical HLT latency budgets, this geometry-aware approach provides a pathway to recover soft, anomalous Beyond Standard Model signatures such as unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs), that routinely evade standard hardware filters.

title: Rank-One Ultralight Dark Matter Response in a Full-Tensor Gravity Gradiometer
abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a $2+2$ pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor $\K=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, with the axis of $\qv$ fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition $\K(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. For copper and lead, the sensitivity reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$, and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers.

title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

title: Performance and Stability Studies of GEM Detectors for High Energy Physics Applications
abstract: R\&D on different gas-filled detectors such as Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs), Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) and straw tubes has been carried out in the detector laboratory of Bose Institute for more than a decade, keeping in mind present and future high-energy physics experiments. In this article, performance studies of a single-mask triple-GEM detector using a $^{55}$Fe X-ray source with an Ar/CO$_2$ (70/30) gas mixture are described. The study focuses mainly on the gain, energy resolution, count rate, and stability of the chamber under long-term irradiation. The experimental setup, methodology, and analysis results are presented.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical features, calorimeter images, and longitudinal shower sequences. Models that follow the longitudinal development of the shower reach the highest accuracy, which points to the value of physically informed representations. The hybrid QLSTM gives the lowest reconstruction error, with an RMSE of 0.294 GeV. Under matched-data conditions with only 1,500 training events, the QLSTM improves on the classical LSTM by 52.7% and also surpasses an LSTM trained on the full set. These observations indicate that longitudinal representations are central to calorimeter energy reconstruction and give preliminary evidence that hybrid quantum-classical sequence models can be more sample-efficient for regression in high-energy physics.

title: MID: a muon detector for the ALICE 3 upgrade project
authors: Jesus Eduardo Mu\~noz Mendez (for the ALICE Collaboration)
abstract: The success of the ALICE programme has allowed to study the hottest state of matter created in the laboratory: the strongly-interacting quark-gluon plasma (sQGP). However, some fundamental questions on the sQGP and other aspects of the strong interaction will remain open even after LHC Run 4. To address this, the ALICE collaboration has proposed a major upgrade of its detector, known as ALICE 3. Among the subdetectors considered for this upgrade is the muon identification detector (MID), whose aim is to contribute to the study of charmonium and exotic-hadron production in heavy-ion collisions. While the baseline design consists of plastic-scintillator-based chambers placed around a cylindrical magnetic iron absorber, different detector technologies are under evaluation for the MID, including multi-wire proportional chambers. This proceeding presents the results of two MID prototypes based on FNAL-NICADD scintillator bars, Kuraray fibers and Hamamatsu SiPMs, characterized in test beams at the CERN Proton Synchrotron with 3 GeV/$c$ muon- and pion-enriched beams. The muon efficiency as well as the hadron suppression obtained using machine learning techniques will be discussed.

title: Observation of Non-Equilibrium Phonon Loss Across a Solid-Superfluid Interface
abstract: We measure the performance of an athermal phonon calorimeter in vacuum and in thermal contact with superfluid $^4$He. Using a cryogenic photon calibration system, we show that the superfluid suppresses the collection of the phonon signal by over 99\%. We conclude that submerged sensors will not benefit TESSERACT's superfluid helium dark matter target, but that superfluid helium may be useful to superconducting qubits as a sink for athermal phonons generated by radiation and other spontaneous sources. Our measurement is the first probe of solid-to-superfluid phonon transmission at energies higher than those stably supportable by the superfluid. We discuss thermal flow inside the calorimeter, as well as systematics from an alternative calibration scheme.

title: A Double Sided LGAD-Based Detector Providing Timing, Position, and Track Angle Information
abstract: We describe a detector concept which combines small pixels enabled by 3D sensor-electronics integration with gain produced by a Low Gain Avalanche Diode (LGAD) layer. The detector is double-sided, with electrons collected by the cathode, which provides timing information, and an anode with small pixels to provide position and angle information. The cathode can be coarse grained, providing timing with fewer fast amplifiers to limit power consumption. The anode layer benefits from the gain of the LGAD, with larger signals that also limit the power needed. Position can be reconstructed by measuring the pattern of total charge deposited on the anode. Angle and depth of charge deposit can be measured by the shapes of the anode pulses. We describe a possible assembly technology based on 3D integration.

title: Real-time Electron Tagging by Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy in the PTOLEMY experiment
abstract: The PTOLEMY project aims at measuring the neutrino mass and, in the future, the Cosmic Neutrino Background from Tritium endpoint measurement. The Radio-Frequency (RF) Tracker is a sub-detector with the goal of measuring in real time the electrons by exploiting the Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy. In this work, an overview of the PTOLEMY project is given together with the design, simulation, construction and commissioning of the RF Tracker prototype: the Electron Trap. The measurements and data analysis of the Electron Trap are presented, establishing the primary path for the development of the RF Tracker.

title: Construction and Commissioning of the Warwick TPC Platform
abstract: Active-target gas time projection chambers (TPCs) could provide the ultimate measurements of neutrino interactions needed for future neutrino oscillation measurements. Their development requires optimisation of the gas mixture, pressure, electric fields, and readout configuration. Warwick TPC (WarTPC) is an R\&D platform for investigating in these directions for neutrino physics and beyond. It can operate at pressures up to approximately 10 bar and features a combination of thick gas electron multipliers and a Timepix3 camera for optical readout. In this paper, we present the construction and commissioning of the WarTPC platform, describing the design and integration of its subsystems, and report the first measurements of its optical response under different operating conditions, demonstrating a stable and functioning R&D platform.

title: Baryon and lepton asymmetries across the cosmic QCD transition: effects of a 3D first-order surface
abstract: We investigate the cosmological QCD phase transition by calculating the cosmic trajectories from the five equations that impose the conservation of the baryon and lepton asymmetries, the charge neutrality of the Universe, and $\beta$ equilibrium. We perform the calculation using for the first time the four-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q, \mu_S)$ Constant Entropy Contour equation of state, which for $\mu_S = 0$ ($\beta$-equilibrium) features a critical line and a first-order phase transition (FOPT) surface in the three-dimensional $(T, \mu_B, \mu_Q)$ space. We first show that, within the standard cosmological scenario with baryon asymmetry $b_{\text{obs}}=8.65\cdot 10^{-11}$, the lepton asymmetries alone can never induce a FOPT. We then explore the non-standard cosmological scenario with large values of $b$ and find that reaching a FOPT requires $b\gtrsim0.028$ during the QCD epoch. Such a value is compatible with observations only if the baryon asymmetry is diluted to $b_{\text{obs}}$ after the transition, which a period of little inflation would provide with $N\approx6.5$ $e$-folds of expansion. Finally, we study the phenomenological imprints on the equation of state and primordial black hole (PBH) formation, showing that pion condensation at large lepton asymmetries drives $c_s^2 > 1/3$ and shifts the PBH peak to sub-solar masses ($0.3-0.8\,M_\odot$), while the large-$b$ FOPT yields a narrow spike around $4.2\,M_\odot$.

title: Microscopic Realizability of Non-unique Bubble Hydrodynamics
abstract: First-order phase transitions drive fluid motion that induces energy transport and gravitational-wave production. The flows are usually classified in terms of the wall velocity and the transition strength. We show that this description fails when the two phases have unequal sound speeds $c_\pm$. New mixed-hybrid profiles may appear, and for a strong hierarchy, $c_+\gg c_-$, where the phase behind the wall is much softer, heating or cooling ahead of the wall allow for the coexistence of distinct stationary flows at the same wall velocity and transition strength. This ambiguity is removed once thermodynamic normalization and entropy production are specified. We identify microscopic settings that realize these sound-speed hierarchies. In thermal plasmas it requires exponentially large mass-to-temperature ratios, whereas at finite density a conserved charge removes this obstruction, making dense matter its natural arena.

title: Unitarity bounds and sum rules in the SMEFT: a systematic analysis
abstract: We present a systematic analysis of perturbative unitarity bounds and spinning sum rules in the baryon-number-conserving dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), with particular emphasis on flavor structure. Employing an on-shell partial-wave formalism for generic $N \to M$ scattering amplitudes, we perform a coupled-channel analysis of the complete operator basis and derive bounds on individual Wilson coefficients by marginalizing over the remaining interactions. We formulate spinning sum rules for four-fermion operators in the Warsaw basis and translate their flavor-space definiteness conditions into constraints on Wilson coefficients, under specified assumptions about the ultraviolet dynamics. We then extend both analyses to the three-generation four-fermion sector within Minimal Flavor Violation, retaining leading up-type Yukawa insertions, and an exact $U(2)^5$ flavor symmetry. The resulting constraints reveal correlations among flavor structures that are absent in the single-flavor limit. Through explicit matching to representative ultraviolet completions, we illustrate how spinning sum rules can distinguish scalar- from vector-mediated interactions, while also identifying the limitations of this interpretation. These results provide a general framework for assessing the consistency of new-physics scenarios within the SMEFT, relying on minimal theoretical assumptions.

title: Positivity Bounds, Negative Running, and the Weak Gravity Conjecture
abstract: We study causality and unitarity constraints at one loop on a low-energy effective theory containing a photon, a massless scalar coupled to it through dilaton-like interactions, and a light neutral Dirac fermion with a Yukawa coupling to the scalar. In this setup, non-gravitational loop effects induced by the Yukawa interaction can drive the coefficient of the four-photon $(F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu})^2$ operator negative at low energies, apparently violating the tree-level positivity bound. Nevertheless, we find that these negative values are consistent with one-loop constraints from causality and unitarity, thanks to the low-energy contribution from the massless scalar to the relevant dispersion relation. We also examine the implications of this negative running for the Weak Gravity Conjecture in the magnetic limit of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes, since the RG-evolved Wilson coefficients can a priori shift the extremality condition towards the subextremal region. We find, however, that this shift is obstructed by the fermion mass induced by the same Yukawa coupling, which prevents the fermion from contributing to the running of the relevant operators down to the low-energy scales required to make the black holes subextremal. Finally, we discuss the relevance of negative running to loop-level positivity bounds in the SMEFT and to light-by-light scattering in the presence of a light scalar.

title: Hydr\'oDex: gotta match 'em all!
abstract: We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic classification of stationary fluid profiles in first-order phase transitions within the constant-sound-speed model, a physically motivated extension of the standard bag model that allows the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the bubble wall and evolving the profile in the surrounding plasma, we systematically identify and classify all the possible stationary solutions. The classification recovers all previously known direct and inverse detonation, deflagration, and hybrid solutions, while revealing a new class of stationary configurations, termed mixed hybrids, featuring rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+ > c_-$, the classification in terms of the wall velocity $\xi_w$ and the asymptotic strength parameter $\alpha_N$ further exhibits degenerate regions in parameter space, where multiple distinct stationary profiles correspond to the same physical inputs $(\xi_w,\alpha_N)$. This non-uniqueness arises as the parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We also compute the kinetic-energy budget and the associated acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed-hybrid solutions, despite their oppositely directed flows, introduce no additional spectral feature, and their spectra can be closely mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with very different fluid profiles. Finally, we release Hydr\'oDex, a public code that implements the complete hydrodynamic classification, fluid-profile construction, kinetic-energy budget, and gravitational-wave calculation.

title: What Comes Out Of Monopole-Fermion Scattering?
abstract: We describe what happens when chiral fermions scatter off magnetic monopoles. It has long been known that, in many situations, the outgoing state cannot be constructed from any finite number of excitations. In the language of 2d CFT, it lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space. Here we explain what this means from the perspective of a d=3+1 observer. We show that an ingoing one-particle excitation is scattered into an outgoing state surrounded by a soft cloud which consists of an infinite number of low energy particle-anti-particle pairs. We compute energy and charge correlators, showing that this cloud fragments in any measurement. A detector will register one or more hard particles which leave tracks and carry standard quantum numbers. The remaining exotic quantum numbers live in the soft cloud, and are characterised by large charge fluctuations in the detector

title: Subleading beauty effects in Higgs production at small transverse momentum
abstract: We study $b$-quark mass effects at small Higgs transverse momentum $q_T$ where the Higgs is produced in gluon fusion via a closed $b$-quark loop. In contrast to top-quark loops, which can be integrated out at a high scale, the $b$-quark mass, $m_b$, induces a second small scale $m_b \sim q_T \ll m_H$ such that standard $q_T$ resummation does not apply in this region, which includes the peak of the distribution. The resummation of mass effects for the $gg\to H$ form factor, which has been studied previously, applies to the $q_T$ spectrum in the limit $q_T \ll m_b$. Unlike this case, for $q_T \sim m_b$, real emissions can resolve the $b$-quark loop, requiring a more complicated simultaneous $m_b$ and $q_T$ factorization. It involves new next-to-leading-power $m_b$ and $q_T$ dependent beam and soft functions, and the corresponding bare factorization theorem suffers - as expected - from endpoint divergences. We use soft-collinear effective theory to explicitly compute all amplitudes with a $b$-quark loop and an additional real soft or collinear emission. Our results provide important insight into the nontrivial structure of the endpoint divergences and show how their expected cancellation happens in the sum of all amplitudes separately for soft and collinear emissions. Interestingly, we find that at this order the endpoint-divergent contributions have a separable dependence on $q_T$ and $m_b$, providing strong motivation that in the future their cancellations can be made manifest in the factorized cross section. As an important further cross check we show that the sum of all SCET amplitudes correctly reproduces the full-QCD one-emission amplitudes expanded in the relevant soft or collinear limit, which also requires nontrivial contributions involving massive Glauber quarks in the effective-theory calculation.

title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $\Delta \chi^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM at $4.1\sigma$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.

title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

title: Geometric Bounds on Axion-Photon Couplings in Non-Supersymmetric Heterotic Compactifications
abstract: We study the photon couplings of QCD axions and axion-like particles in non-supersymmetric heterotic string theory on Calabi-Yau threefolds with line bundles. After the St\"uckelberg mechanism and anomaly matching are taken into account, the QCD axion direction is determined by the QCD axion-coupling coefficients together with the axion kinetic matrix. We focus on the electromagnetic-to-color axion coupling ratio, $E/N$. When the physical electromagnetic and QCD axion-coupling vectors are proportional with the ratio fixed by the gauge levels, the QCD axion has $E/N=8/3$ for $k_3=k_2=1$ and $k_Y=5/3$, independently of the axion kinetic matrix. It is found that direct flux breaking of the visible $SO(16)_{\rm v}$ can produce independent QCD and electromagnetic axion-coupling vectors for the same level assignment. The Hermitian Yang-Mills equations and the heterotic Bianchi identity then restrict the departure from $8/3$. We derive analytic bounds for backgrounds with and without five-brane charge under assumptions about the axion kinetic terms and low-energy matching. An $SU(5)$-like model and a direct-flux Standard-Model-like model illustrate proportional and independent Green-Schwarz coupling vectors, respectively. For axions with no QCD coupling, we derive a geometric upper bound on their photon couplings and evaluate it in an explicit compactification.

title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

title: Searching for signatures of criticality in heavy-ion collisions using two-pion correlation functions
abstract: We study possible signatures of the existence of a Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) critical end-point in low-energy relativistic heavy-ion collisions using two-pion femtoscopy. We simulate central $^{209}\mathrm{Bi}+^{209}\mathrm{Bi}$ collisions at center-of-mass energies ranging from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.8$ to 11 GeV using the EPOS 4.0.3 framework, incorporating an equation of state that explicitly includes a critical end-point and is compatible with lattice QCD results at small baryon chemical potentials. We analyze the pion pair-distance distribution and the corresponding two-pion correlation function by fitting them with L\'evy distributions in configuration and momentum spaces, respectively. We find a weak dependence of the source parameters on the collision energy below $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2$ GeV, followed by a change in trend at higher energies, particularly in the intercept parameter $\lambda$. This behavior may be associated with a decreasing fraction of pions coming from the core and an increasing contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Within the present analysis, we do not identify an unambiguous signal attributable to the critical end-point. A comparison with simulations employing different equation of state parameters to vary the strength of the critical point, as well as with simulations without a critical end-point, is necessary to establish the sensitivity of these observables to critical phenomena.

title: Spin asymmetry in vacuum pair production under polarized electric fields
abstract: We study spin-resolved electron--positron pair production from the quantum vacuum in spatially homogeneous, time-dependent electric fields with linear, elliptical, and circular polarizations. The equal-time Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner formalism is employed to compute the final momentum distributions in two distinct frequency regimes, for both unchirped and chirped field configurations. In the high-frequency regime, characterized by a reference Keldysh parameter, linearly polarized fields yield identical particle yields for the two spin projections considered, whereas elliptical and circular polarizations generate pronounced spin-resolved population imbalances near the dominant multiphoton resonance. Frequency chirping broadens the resonant spectral structures and extends the momentum range over which a sizable normalized spin difference persists. In the low-frequency regime, the pair-production spectra are governed by quantum tunneling and temporal interference effects. Although the peak spin asymmetry in this regime is substantially weaker than in the high-frequency case, the normalized differential spectra still exhibit sign-changing interference fringes. We find that the spin-asymmetry degree exceeds 90$\%$ for circular polarization in the high-frequency regime, while it saturates at approximately 20$\%$ in the low-frequency regime. Given the purely electric background field, we interpret these results in terms of spin-projected Wigner components and the handed time dependence of rotating electric fields, while clearly distinguishing normalized spectral differences from local or integrated polarization observables.

title: Emerging understanding of the rare kaon decay $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$ from lattice QCD
abstract: Rare kaon decays provide sensitive probes of the Standard Model and potential new physics. For $K^+\to\pi^+\ell^+\ell^-$, the experimental decay rate determines only the squared vector form factor $|V(z)|^2$, leaving its sign undetermined. Previous lattice QCD calculations have either used unphysical pion masses or suffered from uncertainties too large to resolve this sign. Here we present a first-principles calculation using two domain-wall fermion ensembles with near-physical pion masses. We develop a computational strategy that establishes the ultraviolet finiteness and continuum equivalence of local and conserved vector currents, substantially simplifying the calculation of nonlocal matrix elements. Four independent subtraction schemes provide nontrivial consistency checks, while the one-end trick reduces noise from quark-self-loop contributions. We determine $V(z)$ at six spacelike and timelike momentum transfers. Fits consistently yield $V(0)<0$, with a statistical significance of $5.8\sigma$--$7.9\sigma$ at $M_{\eta_c}=1.1,\mathrm{GeV}$. After extrapolation to the physical charm-quark mass, the negative sign persists across all fit forms, with a significance of $2.0\sigma$--$3.4\sigma$. Our results provide direct first-principles evidence favoring the negative-sign solution and establish a framework for more precise lattice QCD determinations.

title: Novel observables for exploring jet quenching effects in individual jets
abstract: We introduce event-shape observables in the jet frame to characterize intra-jet shapes and study medium modifications in heavy-ion collisions. Using the JEWEL model, we investigate jet constituent angular and transverse momentum distributions, together with two representative event-shape observables, transverse thrust $\tau_\perp$ and transverse sphericity $S_\perp$, in $p$+$p$ and 0--10% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.02\,\mathrm{TeV}$. These observables are evaluated after transforming the jet constituent momenta into the jet frame. The intra-jet shape distributions in Pb+Pb collisions shift toward larger values relative to those in $p$+$p$ collisions, indicating more isotropic distributions of constituent transverse momenta. Comparisons between calculations with and without recoil, along with the dependence on the constituent transverse momentum threshold, indicate that medium response plays an important role in these modifications. These results suggest that jet-frame event-shape observables provide sensitive probes of medium response in jet quenching, complementary to single-particle angular and transverse momentum distributions.

title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

title: Holographic Butterfly Velocity and Heavy-Quark Drag in a Doubly Anisotropic Magnetized QGP
abstract: We investigate butterfly velocity and heavy-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma with two distinct sources of anisotropy, generated by collision geometry and an external magnetic field, within a five-dimensional holographic model exhibiting magnetic catalysis. In contrast to studies restricted to isotropic or singly anisotropic media, we analyze the butterfly velocity and heavy-quark drag force along all three orthogonal spatial directions at finite temperature and chemical potential in the deconfined phase. We find that the collision-induced anisotropy plays a dominant role in the directional dependence of both butterfly velocity and heavy-quark drag. It governs the directional splitting of the butterfly velocity, and significantly enhances the parallel drag force while suppressing the transverse components. For butterfly velocity, a strong magnetic field primarily suppresses the longitudinal butterfly velocity while leaving the transverse components nearly unchanged. For the drag force, the magnetic field breaks the transverse symmetry, yet it does not alter the overall monotonic increase of the drag force with heavy-quark velocity, temperature, and chemical potential. Most importantly, by bridging the Einstein and string frames via the Weyl transformation, we extract the frame-dependent drag-chaos relation. Generalizing it to the doubly anisotropic plasma, we demonstrate that despite the underlying frame-dependent chaos, the normalized directional drag exhibits a direction-dependent geometric correction at order $\mathcal{O}(v^{3})$. These results establish a direction-resolved connection between heavy-quark dissipation, information scrambling, and the underlying anisotropic geometry of magnetized QGP.

title: Sensitivity to $\Theta^+$ production in the $\pi^- p \to K^- X$ reaction at HIAF-HIRIBL
abstract: Pion-induced searches for the $\Theta^+$ can probe the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation region beyond the E19 energies. We present sensitivity projections for a missing-mass search for a narrow $\Theta^+$ at 1.540 GeV/$c^2$ in $\pi^- p \to K^- X$ at the High Intensity heavy-ion Accelerator Facility and its HIgh-rigidity Radioactive Ion Beam Line. With the E19 resolutions, efficiency, and continuum, separate 10-day exposures at pion momenta of 2.01 and 2.586 GeV/$c$ give background-only median expected 90% CL upper limits of 0.0293 and 0.0356 $\mu$b/sr, respectively, on the differential cross section averaged over $2^\circ$ to $15^\circ$ on the selected high-momentum branch; the higher momentum corresponds to the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation energy. Median local $5\sigma$ discovery thresholds are 0.0894 and 0.109 $\mu$b/sr. Nonresonant nucleon-exchange models give width scales of 0.0039 to 0.079 MeV for $J^P=1/2^+$ and 0.045 to 1.47 MeV for $J^P=1/2^-$. All positive-parity variants would test the DIANA width scale of $0.34 \pm 0.10$ MeV; negative-parity sensitivity depends on the variant.

title: Improved Bounds on the Dark Matter-Neutrino Cross Section using LSBGs
$B \to D$ form factors from light-cone sum rules
abstract: We present a light-cone sum rule (LCSR) analysis of the $B\to D$ transition form factors $f_+^{BD}(q^2)$ and $f_0^{BD}(q^2)$ in the large-recoil region, including the next-to-leading-power corrections at tree level. The non-perturbative input is provided by the leading-twist $D$-meson distribution amplitude determined from lattice QCD in the heavy-quark large-momentum effective theory (HQLaMET) framework, which enters together with the twist-three and twist-four distribution amplitudes of the $D$ meson fixed by the QCD equations of motion. A combined fit to the LCSR results at $q^2\lesssim2$~GeV$^2$ and to the FNAL/MILC and HPQCD lattice data at $q^2\gtrsim8.5$~GeV$^2$, performed in the model-independent Boyd-Grinstein-Lebed (BGL) parametrisation, allows us to obtain the form factors over the whole physical range and to extract $|V_{cb}|$ from the semileptonic $B\to D\ell\nu$ decay as well as the lepton-flavour universality ratio $R(D)$.

title: Gravitational form factors of $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD
abstract: We compute the gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of the $\rho$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD, a holographic model of QCD with backreacting flavor and dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. The parameters of the model are taken from an earlier fit to meson spectra and are not adjusted to form factor data. Both mesons are described by a single spin-1 field, and the six form factors are identified from the matrix element of the energy-momentum tensor with two spin-1 states, following the holographic dictionary. We find that $A_0 = J$ and $A_1 = 0$ hold identically in the model, and show that the remaining form factors $E$, $D_0$ and $D_1$ are regular at zero momentum transfer. We compare the form factors of $\rho$ with results from the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, a light-cone constituent quark model and the hard-wall holographic model. From the form factors, we compute the monopole and quadrupole distributions of energy, pressure and shear force in the Breit frame. The D-term, defined for spin-1 hadrons as the forward value of the combination $\mathcal{D}_0(t)$ of form factors, is found to be $-2.98$ for the $\rho$ and $-7.43$ for the $a_1$ meson. The mass and mechanical radii are $0.81$~fm and $0.89$~fm for $\rho$, and $0.73$~fm and $0.80$~fm for $a_1$.

title: ESME stays positive: event generation with positive weights
abstract: Fully differential simulations of hard-scattering processes are a cornerstone of precision phenomenology at collider experiments. For long, Monte Carlo event generators have been able to achieve next-to-leading order (NLO) accuracy, but their results typically suffer from the presence of negative-weight events. These degrade statistical power and complicate downstream analyses. In this contribution, we present Exponentiated Subtraction for Matching Events (ESME), a novel approach to NLO+PS matching that yields positive-definite event weights while preserving perturbative accuracy and the logarithmic structure of the shower. We discuss the formalism and its implementation within the PanScales framework.

title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
abstract: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.

title: Probing Dirac Heavy Neutral Leptons through EFT-Induced Meson Decays
abstract: We investigate dimension-six operators involving pairs of Dirac-type heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at beam-dump and far-forward experiments. In the $\nu$SMEFT framework, lepton-number-conserving four-fermion operators couple HNL pairs to quarks and induce two and three-body charm and bottom meson decays. We study the $c\to u$, $b\to d$, and $b\to s$ transitions at FASER2, FACET, SHiP, and two FPF@FCC configurations. HNL production depends on the cut-off scale $\Lambda$, while the lifetime depends on the active-sterile mixing $|V_{eN}|^2$. Sizable production can therefore coexist with the small mixing needed for HNLs to reach distant detectors. We project sensitivities in the $(M_N,|V_{eN}|^2)$ and $(M_N,\Lambda)$ planes, accounting for two and three-body decays and constraints from invisible and semivisible meson decays. SHiP is particularly sensitive to $c\to u$, while the larger FCC-LLP2 configuration probes $b\to d, s$. We find that EFT-induced pair production extends long-lived HNL searches to very small mixing and complements other probes of the $\nu$SMEFT heavy-neutrino sector.

title: Efficient Iterative Symmetrization algorithm for quantum computing and hadron applications
abstract: Efficient algorithms for the (anti)symmetrization of quantum registers are necessary for upcoming few- and many-body physics applications, from atomic to particle-physics scales. We propose a recursive algorithm (anti)symmetrizing the last particle added to memory, each time one is created or destroyed, respect to the rest of already (anti)symmetrized ones. Given a generalized Dicke state (GDS) of $(j-1)$ quantum registers, each assigned to a particle, the algorithm produces another GDS of $j$ registers (of $n_{qb}$ qubits each) using a mere $\mathcal{O}(j\log_2^2 j + j n_{qb})$ $\mathtt{CNOT}$ and single-qubit gates, and $3j+\lceil\log_2j\rceil+\mathcal{O}(\max(n_{qb},\log_2 j))$ clean auxiliary qubits. The (anti)symmetrizing operator constructed for this purpose depends on the quantum numbers of the additional particle being introduced or ``created''. The algorithm improves upon the construction presented in Appendix A of \cite{Galvez-Viruet:2024hry} by almost two powers of $j$ and is on par with the most efficient methods to date, while ideally suited for dynamical memory management with variable particle number. We exemplify its applicability with a small selection of problems from hadron physics which are expected to be addressable with upcoming quantum computers.

title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
abstract: The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson. To assess how well quantum state tomography constrains the $hZZ$ anomalous couplings and the trilinear coupling at FCC-ee, we compute the helicity density matrix of the $Z$ boson, for an effective vertex that also includes a CP-odd anomalous coupling $\tilde b_Z$, together with its complete one-loop correction in the Standard Model. With these corrections and no other new physics in the effective vertex, quantum state tomography determines $\kappa_\lambda$ to $\pm 3.9$, or $\pm 2.9$ with the full angular information, independently of the rate and of the normalization of the vertex, and not far from the limit $\delta\kappa_\lambda \simeq 1$ set by the quantum Fisher information. Without assumptions on the new physics, quantum tomography directly bounds the anomalous couplings at the $10^{-3}$ level, improving on the existing projections. The density matrix also characterizes the $Z$ boson as a qutrit. At $365$ GeV its state in the central region is pure enough to violate the Klyachko--Can--Binicio\u{g}lu--Shumovsky contextuality inequality, $\mathbb{CNTXT}_5 = 2.06$ at $\theta = \pi/2$ against the non-contextual bound $2$. We also quantify the purity and the amount of magic of the $Z$ boson state, using the mana, the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy and the robustness of magic for the latter. At fixed angle, purity, contextuality and magic are robust against anomalous couplings of the size probed by the tomography. The inclusive state, instead, is neither contextual in this test nor magic in the helicity basis.

title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
abstract: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. Urca processes in neutron star matter try to restore the system towards equilibrium providing strong bulk viscous damping of these density oscillations. Standard bulk viscosity calculations typically assume small amplitude density oscillations, such that the deviation from chemical equilibrium $\mu_{\Delta}$ is less than the temperature $T$. In this work we compute the complete amplitude dependent bulk viscosity, taking into account, for the first time, thermal blurring effects and collisional broadening of in-medium nucleons. Our results show that the non-linear effects in bulk viscosity start to become important when the oscillation amplitude is about $10$ percent of the background density. In this regime the bulk viscosity can increase by three to five orders of magnitude. These results have important consequences for simulations of binary neutron star mergers as well as their multi-messenger observations.

title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order Prediction for the Radiative $B_{u}^- \to \gamma \ell^{-} \bar \nu_{\ell}$ Decay
abstract: We accomplish for the first time the three-loop computation of the photonic radiative jet function in soft-collinear effective theory, which constitutes the last missing and most difficult ingredient for the complete next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD prediction of the simplest radiative $B_{u}^- \to \gamma \ell^{-} \bar \nu_{\ell}$ decay with an energetic photon at leading power. Importantly, the most prominent three-loop contribution to the radiative bottom-meson decay form factors turns out to arise from the newly determined QCD correction to the jet function rather than from the recently obtained hard correction. We further demonstrate explicitly that our full three-loop calculation of these non-hadronic radiative $B$-meson decay form factors appear to be highly beneficial for an improved extraction of the fundamental shape parameter $\lambda_B$ of the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude.

title: Three-Loop Evolution for Soft Functions of Exclusive $B$-Meson and Higgs Decays
abstract: We bootstrap the complete three-loop Lange--Neubert kernel for the leading-twist $B$-meson light-cone distribution amplitude in heavy quark effective theory by taking advantage of the conformal symmetry technique. In particular, we provide for the first time an all-order Wilson-line argument for the determination of the constant term in the LN kernel in terms of the light-quark, heavy-quark, and threshold soft anomalous dimensions. Remarkably, this innovative construction requires no additional three-loop diagrammatic calculations. Taking into account further the three-loop QCD evolutions for the hard and hard-collinear coefficient functions, the newly derived three-loop Lange--Neubert equation enables us to manifestly demonstrate the renormalization-group invariance of the soft-collinear factorization formula for the radiative leptonic $B_{u}^- \to \gamma \ell^{-} \bar \nu_{\ell}$ decay at leading power, validating our bootstrapped three-loop kernel and more importantly, our full bootstrap approach.

title: RG evolution of the $B$-meson LCDA and radiative jet function at three loops
abstract: We calculate the three-loop evolution kernel of the light-cone distribution amplitude of the $B$ meson, together with the radiative jet function in the leptonic radiative decay $B^-\to\gamma\ell^-\bar\nu$ for the first time. Representing the light-cone distribution amplitude as the discontinuity of a matrix element containing an inverse differential operator, we compute the partonic matrix element in momentum space with a novel method of infrared subtraction. We show that its infrared singularities are governed by the same anomalous dimension as that of the heavy-light quark form factor, so that they can be subtracted without introducing any infrared regulator, thereby preserving gauge invariance and avoiding additional complexity in the Feynman integrals. Based on the renormalization-group invariance of the factorization theorem, we derive the renormalization factor of the radiative jet function, and confirm that it removes all divergences of the bare three-loop radiative jet function. Our results enable the resummation of large logarithms in exclusive $B$ decays at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy.

title: Light baryon masses from the modified Taylor coupling
abstract: We present a calculation of the positive-parity baryon octet and decuplet spectra, using a non-perturbative interaction governed by the modified Taylor effective charge and complemented by explicit flavour-dependent contributions. The framework transitions seamlessly from the mesonic domain, where it was first established, to the baryonic sector, requiring no further parameter optimization. By solving the relativistic three-body Faddeev equation, we extract both the ground-state masses and amplitudes for the corresponding baryonic configurations. The resulting spectrum reproduces experimental data within a few percent. Additionally, we derive the evolution of the nucleon and $\Delta$ masses as functions of the pion mass, contrast our findings directly against lattice-QCD benchmarks, and evaluate the propagation of the lattice uncertainties into the computed hadronic observables.

title: Are hybrid hydrodynamic models missing soft-pion physics?
abstract: In this work, we perform a systematic Bayesian analysis of the full parameter space of a state-of-the-art hybrid hydrodynamical model and show that no combination of parameters provides a satisfactory description of the low-$p_T$ region of the pion $(\pi^{\pm})$ transverse-momentum spectra. This suggests that an additional mechanism enhancing pion production at low $p_T$ may be needed to properly describe the ALICE data. We first reexamine and confirm the existence of an excess of low $p_T$ pions relative to model predictions, showing that no comparable excess is observed in the spectra of kaons $(K^\pm)$, protons $(p)$, or antiprotons $(\bar{p})$. We further demonstrate that this excess persists under a rigorous Bayesian analysis of simulations that include, e.g., a hadronic afterburner, a feature omitted in previous similar studies. Despite the observed excess, the scaled pion spectra retain their universal behavior, exhibiting little dependence on collision centrality. In fact, pions exhibit the most pronounced universality among the particle species considered. We then estimate the effects of two candidate mechanisms for generating the low-$p_T$ pion enhancement by introducing a one-parameter extension of the model into the Bayesian analysis. We find that the data favor enhancement mechanisms whose contributions decrease with increasing $p_T$, becoming negligible at high-$p_T$. Our results motivate further investigations of non-equilibrium effects in hybrid hydrodynamic simulations.

title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
abstract: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_\mu$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $\rho \pi$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.

title: Connecting High-Twist Expansion and Color Glass Condensate Dynamics
abstract: The high-twist (HT) expansion and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) describe nuclear multiple scattering in complementary kinematic regimes. For direct-photon production in proton-nucleus collisions, we formulate an arbitrary-order multiple-scattering master expression that includes photon emission before, between, or after the ordered quark scatterings in the amplitude and its conjugate. In the high-energy limit, resumming multiple scatterings to all orders recovers the CGC Wilson-line dipole result. However, the naive power expansion of the eikonal CGC result reproduces the leading twist but only part of the twist-four contribution obtained in the HT expansion. Including longitudinal sub-eikonal phases and Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal interference restores the CGC-HT correspondence through twist-4.

title: Gravitational production of dark QED by the trace anomaly
abstract: We revisit the production of fermionic dark matter $\chi$ through the graviton portal, sourced by inflaton annihilation at the end of inflation. Because the production rate is helicity-suppressed, $\propto m_\chi^2$, the dark fermion must be very heavy to account for the observed relic abundance, $m_\chi \gtrsim 10^{10}$ GeV, with the exact bound set by the reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH}$. Here we examine how interactions within the dark sector could modify this result. As a toy model, we consider dark QED, in which $\chi$ couples to a light dark photon. We first show that, as a consequence of classical conformal invariance, bremsstrahlung of a dark photon does not lift the helicity suppression for light fermions. We then show that the trace anomaly of dark QED, which affects the coupling of the graviton to dark photons, can produce light dark fermions via a Dalitz process. This allows to extend the fermionic dark mass range possibly down to $m_\chi \sim 10^7$~GeV, depending on $T_{\rm RH}$ and the dark QED coupling. We also determine under which conditions the hidden sector reaches thermal equilibrium and derive a lower bound on the temperature ratio at reheating $(T'/T)_{\rm RH}$ as function of the dark QED coupling and the reheating temperature.

title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
abstract: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/\epsilon$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.

title: Three-dimensional parton structure in QCD with CP-violation
abstract: The Energy-Momentum tensor encodes the mechanical properties of a system such as the internal distributions energy, momentum, forces, and particle fluxes. The QCD energy momentum tensor respects CP symmetry even when QCD is modified with a CP-violating $\theta$-term. In this theory, there are 5 unique generalized form factors in the Lorentz decomposition of the total Energy Momentum tensor and 3 more which only vanish when summing over all flavors. We introduce two new lightcone GPDs whose Mellin moments give the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. These generalize the observables for QCD-based CP violation such as the neutron electric dipole moment to three dimensional light cone structure.

title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $\phi^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
abstract: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $\phi^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.
